title: Canonical proper Frobenius power squares and their mate pasting
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with $p$ prime, $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $k=\overline{k_0}$. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$ and $n\geq1$, and set $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\gamma=(z\mapsto z^q)^{-1}$ and $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of constant-$A$ modules on the small pro-etale sites and their adjoint operations $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. All composition comparisons below are the canonical ones of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]; composition is written with the rightmost map first.

Let $p_0:W_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] with $W_0$ of finite type over $k_0$, and let $p:W=W_0\times_{k_0}k\to s$ be its base change. Put $b=\operatorname{id}_{W_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$, $B_r=L(b^r)^*$, $Q_r=L(h^r)^*$, $L=Lp^*$ and $R=Rp_*$. For $m\geq1$ write $t_m:Q_1Q_m\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{m+1}$ and $d_m:B_1B_m\xrightarrow{\sim}B_{m+1}$ for the inverse composition comparisons. The square with vertical edges $p,p$ and horizontal edges $b^r,h^r$ commutes and is Cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] for each $r\geq1$, with its canonical lift $(b^r,p)$. Let $\theta_r:LQ_r\xrightarrow{\sim}B_rL$ be its square comparison and $u_r:Q_rR\to RB_r$ its ambient exchange, the unit--square--counit mate specified in [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange], equivalently the finite direct-image recipe of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] (1) for power $r$.

Then these specified transformations satisfy
$$\theta_{m+1}\circ L(t_m)=(d_mL)\circ(B_1\theta_m)\circ(\theta_1Q_m),$$
and, for every $K\in D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $m\geq1$,
$$u_{m+1,K}\circ t_{m,RK}=R(d_{m,K})\circ u_{1,B_mK}\circ Q_1(u_{m,K}).$$
The latter equality is natural in $K$ in the ambient derived categories. The horizontal arrows are scheme isomorphisms; no $k$-linearity of those arrows is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0E47, remark-compose-base-change-horizontal, specialized to powers of a fixed Frobenius square. Agent refinement: the canonical left-comparison equation and its mate, with the explicit power-square lift; Deligne Weil II (1.1.10)-(1.1.11) fixes geometric Frobenius.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian] to $p_0$. It gives scheme isomorphisms $b,h$ and $pb=hp$. Induction gives $pb^r=h^rp$; the inverses of $b^r,h^r$ are the corresponding powers of their inverses. For the power square let $P=W\times_{p,s,h^r}s$, with projections $\pi_W,\pi_s$. Its specified lift is $a_r=(b^r,p):W\to P$. Define $v_r=b^{-r}\pi_W:P\to W$. The pullback relation and commutation imply $pv_r=h^{-r}p\pi_W=\pi_s$. Consequently $v_ra_r=1_W$, while the two projections of $a_rv_r$ are $\pi_W,\pi_s$, so $a_rv_r=1_P$ by the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. This proves the Cartesian assertion with exactly the specified lift. This argument takes place in schemes; it uses no $k$-linearity.

source.place: Tag 0E47, remark-compose-base-change-horizontal; Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition. Agent specialization to the specified Frobenius powers.

proof.text: The coefficient ring $A$ is a finite commutative ring: the extended absolute value is nonarchimedean by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value], its valuation ring is a DVR with finite residue field by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], and [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] applies to the given uniformizer and $n\geq1$. The canonical constant coefficient identifications compose by [lem-trf-constant-coefficient-composition]. Thus the coefficient and category hypotheses of the next step hold on the ordinary unbounded derived categories in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0E47, remark-compose-base-change-horizontal; Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition. Agent specialization to the specified Frobenius powers.

proof.text: Use [lem-pur-factorized-pullback-square-pasting] with $u=p$, $(r_X,r_Y)=(b,h)$ and $(s_X,s_Y)=(b^m,h^m)$. The commuting relations are step 1. Its $P_u$ is $L$, its $C_r,C_s,C_t$ are $\theta_1,\theta_m,\theta_{m+1}$ by the explicit compositor formula in [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange], and its $d_Y,d_X$ are $t_m^{-1},d_m^{-1}$. Indeed $s_Tr_T$ is the $(m+1)$-st power; the cited pasting statement includes the transports along these equalities. Its equation therefore reads $S_m\circ L(t_m^{-1})=(d_m^{-1}L)\circ\theta_{m+1}$, where $S_m=(B_1\theta_m)\circ(\theta_1Q_m)$. Precompose by $L(t_m)$ and postcompose by $d_mL$. The inverse pairs cancel, giving $\theta_{m+1}\circ L(t_m)=(d_mL)\circ S_m$, exactly the first required identity. All functors and comparisons here are the specified ones, not independently chosen isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0E47, remark-compose-base-change-horizontal; Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition. Agent specialization to the specified Frobenius powers.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange], the mate of each $\theta_r$ under the specified adjunction $L\dashv R$ at both vertical sides is $u_r$. Apply clause 1 of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] with all three vertical adjunctions equal to $L\dashv R$, $\alpha=\theta_m$, $\beta=\theta_1$, $G=Q_m$, $H=B_m$, $G_2=Q_1$, $H_2=B_1$. It gives $S_m^\flat=(u_1B_m)\circ Q_1(u_m):Q_1Q_mR\to RB_1B_m$. This fixes the order of the two exchanges without replacing the ambient mate by an abstractly isomorphic base-change map.

source.place: Tag 0E47, remark-compose-base-change-horizontal; Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition. Agent specialization to the specified Frobenius powers.

proof.text:
Take mates of the equality in step 3. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-mate-whisker] on the left with $\alpha=\theta_{m+1}$, $\sigma=t_m:Q_1Q_m\to Q_{m+1}$ and $\tau=1_{B_{m+1}}$: its mate is $u_{m+1}\circ(t_mR)$. Apply it on the right with $\alpha=S_m$, $\sigma=1_{Q_1Q_m}$ and $\tau=d_m:B_1B_m\to B_{m+1}$: its mate is $(Rd_m)\circ S_m^\flat$. Equality is preserved because taking mates is a function on natural transformations. Substitute step 4 and evaluate at $K$ to obtain
$$u_{m+1,K}\circ t_{m,RK}=R(d_{m,K})\circ u_{1,B_mK}\circ Q_1(u_{m,K}).$$
The calculation is an equality of natural transformations before evaluation, so it also proves naturality in $K$ on the whole ambient derived category. No boundedness or constructibility hypothesis has been introduced.
